author: Härtel
asr_identification: Sonkh mound, 14 miles (c. 25 km by road) SW of Mathura, Mathura district, Uttar Pradesh (27°24' N, 77°30' E)
evidence: German excavation 1966–74 chose a less disturbed mound outside Mathura city rather than the city itself; 40 habitation levels from the 8th c. BC (PGW) to the 19th c.; Kushan apsidal Nāga temple. In eight seasons nothing Buddhist was found at Sonkh, so the reported Sonkh provenance of a Cakravartin Buddha dated Kaniṣka 23 is doubted. The ancient name of the site is unknown. No mention of Xuanzang or Faxian, of the Katra or of the Dhulkot.
quote: vation of a less disturbed mound outside of…Mathura would be more promising than a…place in the city itself…paigns of excavations nothing Buddhistic…has been found in this site
note: Not about the location of Mathurā or its monasteries; Sonkh is a provincial town in the Mathurā country with no Buddhist remains. Does not bear on the study's or Mizutani's identification (Mathura, ancient city within the Dhulkot).

author: Härtel
asr_identification: Sonkh mound, Mathura district, Uttar Pradesh
evidence: Stratigraphy: Level 16 (Vāsudeva I and successors) is the last well-built level; Level 15/14 Gupta (terracotta Makara relief of Gaṅgā, moulded sherds, black-striped red jars); Levels 14–12 'in all probability' Post-Gupta and Early Medieval, undated by coins, with destruction by conflagration, devastation and decay, poor houses of brickbats and grey stone plaques of Hindu deities for domestic worship; then abandonment of Level 12 before the Level 11 caravanserai (10th c. or Delhi Sultanate).
quote: Levels 14 to 12 belong in all…probability to Post Gupta and Early Me…inextricable in view of the strong signs of…struction caused by conflagration, de…vastation and decay
note: Context only: a shrunken, Hindu, post-Gupta settlement at Sonkh in roughly Xuanzang's time; says nothing about Mathurā city or its saṅghārāmas. No bearing on the identification.

author: Aboshi et al.
name_in_asr: Maheth (Sravasti); マヘ-ト遺跡(舎衛城)
asr_identification: Maheth (Mahet), the walled city of Sahet-Mahet, on the Rapti, Shravasti district, Uttar Pradesh
evidence: Kansai University–ASI excavations 1994–97 at Maheth, taken as the city of Śrāvastī. Area A (S of the Surajkund): nine phases of pits on natural soil, c. 500–100 BC, iron, non-ferrous metal and glass workshops (not the 'palace area' first supposed). Area B (NE rampart, 55 m trench): earthen rampart c. 40 m wide and 8.5 m high; Period I built c. 250 BC (Mauryan), major rebuild c. 50 BC (Śuṅga), brick parapet on top; repaired to c. AD 100 (Kushan), then left unused to the present; the abandonment of the wall coincides with the rapid decline of the whole site in the later Kushan period. Wall circuit c. 5.23 km. The philological team compares inscribed finds with Buddhist texts on the Jetavana and the city. Summary published 9 Mar 1999.
quote: 全長約5.23kmに及ぶ城壁の東北部分(B地区)を中心に発掘しました。…その第I期は紀元前250年頃(マウリヤ朝期)に構築され、紀元前50年頃(シュンガ朝期)に大改修を受けたことを確認しました。…なお、城壁の放棄は関連遺構の遺存状態から推測できるマヘ-ト遺跡全体の急速な衰退期(クシャン朝後半期)と、ほぼその時期が一致していることに注目できます。
note: Agrees with the study and Mizutani (Sahet-Mahet, high): takes Maheth = Śrāvastī as settled; adds stratified dates for the rampart (c. 250 BC–AD 100) and a late-Kushan decline of the city, in keeping with the deserted city Xuanzang describes (though the summary does not say so). The 5.23 km circuit matches Cunningham's and Vogel's c. 17,300 ft against Xuanzang's 20 li. No new inscription naming the city.

author: Aboshi et al.
name_in_asr: Maheth (Sravasti); マヘ-ト遺跡(舎衛城)
asr_identification: Maheth (Mahet), Area C in the N half of the walled city, Shravasti district, Uttar Pradesh
evidence: Area C (1996–97), the supposed town quarter in the N half: a brick well c. 6 m across and over 6 m deep, the largest at the site, cut through Śuṅga deposits (built around the turn of the era; the English summary says earliest stage Kushan), used to medieval times; brick buildings around it from the Kushan to the medieval period. About 50 m W of the well a large brick building with decorated (moulded-brick) outer walls, judged a Gupta-period assembly hall (English: 'after Late Gupta'), repaired and used to medieval times and later.
quote: この建造物は外壁面に装飾煉瓦を組み込んだ特異な壁面構成を示しており、その構造や出土遺物を勘案した場合、グプタ朝期に建造された集会場と推断することができます。その後、この集会場は改修築を受けながら、中世期以降まで使用されていたことが判明しています。
note: Agrees; adds that part of the N half of Maheth was still occupied in Gupta and post-Gupta times (cf. L. C. Singh's late-Gupta 'shrunk settlement' near the Surajkund, IAR 1993–94), so Xuanzang's ruined city was not wholly empty. The two summaries differ on the hall's date (ja Gupta, en after Late Gupta); the full report would settle it. No change to the rating.
